description: ABO + Rh blood groups, donor/recipient compatibility

options.option_text: O negative (no antigens, can give to all)

questions.explanation: ABO BLOOD TYPING: discovered by KARL LANDSTEINER (1900, Nobel 1930) — saved millions via safe transfusions. 4 types (A, B, AB, O) based on ANTIGENS on RBCs. Plus Rh factor (+ or −). O- (O negative) — NO antigens (A, B, or Rh) → no immune response in any recipient → UNIVERSAL DONOR. AB+ — has all antigens → no foreign antigens to fight → UNIVERSAL RECIPIENT. SAFE transfusion: donor's RBC antigens shouldn't trigger recipient's antibodies. INDIA: B+ most common (~32%), then O+ (~28%); O- rarest (~3%). DONATION SAVES: 1 unit donated → 3 lives. ELIGIBILITY: 18-65 yrs, 50+ kg, healthy. India needs ~12M units annually.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.explanation: AB+ — has BOTH A and B antigens, plus Rh+ — recipient has NO antibodies against A, B, or Rh → can SAFELY receive blood from any donor (A, B, AB, O; + or −). RECIPROCAL of universal donor logic. AB+ patients can take O-, A+, B+, AB+ — anything works. AB+ blood is rare (~5% of population). PARADOX: AB+ can RECEIVE from anyone; AB+ can DONATE only to AB+. ANTIGENS = surface markers on RBCs (proteins/glycoproteins); ANTIBODIES = floating in plasma; antigens-antibodies of MISMATCHED type → AGGLUTINATION (clumping) → fatal. CRITICAL: ALWAYS CROSSMATCH before transfusion to verify compatibility.

questions.stem: Rh FACTOR was named after which animal?

options.option_text: Rhesus monkey (where it was first found)

questions.explanation: Rh FACTOR — named after RHESUS MONKEY (Macaca mulatta). Discovered (1937, Landsteiner + Wiener) when antibodies in human blood reacted with rhesus monkey RBC antigens. Rh+ have antigen on RBCs; Rh− don't. ~85% of people are Rh+; 15% Rh−. Rh− mother + Rh+ baby → mother's body may produce ANTI-Rh antibodies (esp. 2nd pregnancy onwards); these cross placenta → attack baby's RBCs → HEMOLYTIC DISEASE OF NEWBORN (HDN / erythroblastosis fetalis). PREVENTION: ANTI-D INJECTION (Rho-GAM) given to Rh− mothers within 72 hrs of childbirth; suppresses anti-Rh formation. SOCIAL: pre-marital blood-typing recommended in some traditions to predict compatibility issues.

questions.stem: Person with blood group A has which antigen + antibody?

options.option_text: A antigen on RBC + anti-B antibody in plasma
B antigen on RBC + anti-A antibody

questions.explanation: Blood Group A: A antigen on RBCs; ANTI-B antibody in plasma (since body's anti-A would attack own A-antigen — auto-immune; only anti-B is safe to keep). Blood Group B: B antigen + anti-A antibody. Blood Group AB: A AND B antigens; NO antibodies (otherwise would attack own RBCs). Blood Group O: NO A or B antigens; BOTH anti-A AND anti-B antibodies. INHERITANCE: ABO determined by ALLELES of one gene (Iᴬ, Iᴮ, i — co-dominant for A,B; recessive for O). PARENTS A+B → kids can be A, B, AB, or O (depending on alleles). Parents both O → kids only O. INSIGHT — same logic for KARL LANDSTEINER discovery: identifying which combos are safe = bedrock of modern transfusion medicine.

questions.stem: Number of CHROMOSOMES in normal human body cells (somatic):
questions.explanation: HUMAN body (somatic) cells = DIPLOID = 46 chromosomes (23 pairs): 22 pairs AUTOSOMES + 1 pair SEX CHROMOSOMES (XX female; XY male). GAMETES (sperm + egg) = HAPLOID = 23 (one of each pair). FERTILISATION restores 46 (23 + 23). DOWN SYNDROME = trisomy 21 (3 copies of chr 21 → 47 chromosomes total). KLINEFELTER (XXY = 47), TURNER (X0 = 45). HUMAN GENOME PROJECT (1990-2003) sequenced ~3 BILLION base pairs across 46 chromosomes; ~20,000 genes (less than predicted). MITOCHONDRIAL DNA: separate, inherited only from MOTHER. INSIGHT — chromosome count varies by species: dog 78, cat 38, horse 64, elephant 56, rice 24, mouse 40, fly 8, mosquito 6 — number doesn't correlate with complexity!

questions.stem: Which sex chromosome combination is FEMALE?
questions.explanation: FEMALE = XX. MALE = XY. Y chromosome carries SRY GENE that triggers male development. INHERITED — egg always X (mother only has X); sperm carries X (→ daughter) or Y (→ son). FATHER DETERMINES BABY'S SEX. INSIGHT — historic injustice of blaming mothers for not having sons (esp. India): biologically wrong; sex is determined by sperm chromosome, controlled by father. KING HENRY VIII famously beheaded 2 wives over not bearing sons — biologically his fault, not theirs! ABNORMAL: X0 (TURNER, female, 45 chr — short stature, infertile); XXY (KLINEFELTER, male, 47 chr — often infertile); XXX (TRIPLE X, female); XYY (Jacob's syndrome). 'PRESERVATION OF DAUGHTERS' campaigns ('Beti Bachao Beti Padhao') important in India given historic gender bias.

questions.stem: Most common blood group in INDIA is:
questions.explanation: INDIA's blood group distribution (approximate): B+ ~32%, O+ ~28%, A+ ~21%, AB+ ~8%, Negative groups ~5-7% combined (O- ~3%, A- ~2%, B- ~2%, AB- ~1%). VARIES by region: South India has more O+; North India has more B+. GLOBAL: O+ is most common worldwide (~38%); India is unusual for high B+ frequency. Rh− is rare in Asia (~5-7%) compared to Europe (~15%) — selection pressure related to malaria likely explains. RARE Rh BLOOD: 'Bombay phenotype' (Hh) — discovered in Mumbai 1952 by YM Bhende; people lack H antigen; can ONLY receive blood from another Bombay phenotype donor; very rare (~1 in 10,000 in India). National Blood Transfusion Council + state blood banks coordinate supply.
